commander: Major General Charles C. Haffner, Jr.
current_activity: first combat: two regiments cross the Meurthe at the 3rd Division sites
notes: Event date: 20 November 1944 (Riviera p396: late on 20 November Brooks decided to send two regiments of the 103d Division over the Meurthe at the 3d Division's crossing sites; p391: the 100th and 103d Divisions were entering combat for the first time). Event definition: the 103rd Division's first combat is the Meurthe crossing; the order is dated late on 20 November so the crossing itself was on or just after that date. Relationship: VI Corps, Seventh Army and 6th Army Group (CMH table, from 6 November). Location: Division command post at Les Rouges-Eaux on 19 November (atlas), the day before. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Les Rouges-Eaux. Event support: moderate (decision dated, crossing time not). Location support: moderate (command post listed one day earlier).

current_activity: command post at Innsbruck as the 411th Infantry reaches the Brenner Pass
notes: Event date: 4 May 1945 (Last Offensive ch. 19 p. 468-469: Austrian partisans seized control of Innsbruck during 2 May; the 103d Division still had to fight through delaying groups to reach the city; its 411th Infantry took the town of Brenner just before 0200 on 4 May and a mounted patrol made contact at 1051 with reconnaissance troops of the 88th Infantry Division at Vipiteno; CMH ETO-OB command-post list of the 103d Infantry Division: Innsbruck on 4 May 45). Event definition: the command post is at the Tyrolean capital on the day a regiment reaches the Italian frontier. Relationship: VI Corps unspecified_subordination (from 19 Apr 45, CMH table); Seventh Army assigned (from 1 Nov 44, CMH table); 6th Army Group assigned (from 1 Nov 44, CMH table). The table entries start on the first row of the unbroken run (convention V-013). The CMH table has a single corps column and does not say assigned or attached for a corps. The earlier unspecified_subordination relation to VI Corps (CR0362) is closed at 28 March 1945 (inferred_from_next_claim); see the Review note on it. Location: Innsbruck (CMH ETO-OB command-post list, R338 p. 406: listed 4 May 1945); the town centre stands for the command post. Coordinates: Wikipedia (en): Innsbruck. Event support: moderate (one Green Book chapter, the CMH table and the CMH Combat Chronicle). Location support: moderate (command post listed on the date). Review (27 October 2026, found while checking this row against a source not used to write it): the CMH Combat Chronicle of the division (R583) says the division "took Innsbruck on 3 May and reached the Brenner Pass on the 4th"; the command-post list has Innsbruck on 4 May. The row is the command post on 4 May and the Brenner event; the day the division first entered Innsbruck is 3 May by the Chronicle and is not a separate row. The Chronicle also lists VI Corps from 19 April, as the CMH table does.
